disposition: Declared Seti/Original notice and transformation boundary characterized; named missing third-party Ruby source/notice remains unresolved, with separate publication and execution obligations.
convention: SHA256 is over exact HTTP response bytes or UTF-8 source file bytes, with LF/CRLF and final newline preserved; ranges use 1-based inclusive lines and 0-based half-open byte offsets. API evidence uses response SHA256 plus JSON pointer and immutable commit IDs; Git blob joins compare content identities, not publisher signatures. SVG whole-file fingerprints and declaration scans are not geometry, authorship, legal or build-correctness proof.

scope.historyLimit: Five scoped path-history queries (four max8, one max3), one documentation commit and a bounded five-commit import ancestry segment; one extra immediate parent was read and stopped at unrelated CI. No per-glyph history loop or unrelated repository census.
scope.metadataReview: Fetched only the 191 icons.tsv-selected current SVGs and scanned origin/notice/header declarations; retained whole-file fingerprints. Geometry was not semantically compared across all glyphs; title/Sketch/Inkscape metadata cannot establish a rights grant.

resolved.finding: Nerd commit 4ada58a6607160e8006cb6ab4de168a6081998c4 expressly names Seti fd20793e5a75b350eab8d489165fb9b420df3f62; all168 added src/seti SVG blob identities equal that revision's icons members. Upstream package declares1.11.0; v0.8.1 is no longer the asserted import origin.

Seti source notice is Copyright(c)2014 Jesse Weed, full MIT permission/condition/disclaimer. Nerd root declares original code/default source MIT with Copyright(c)2014 Ryan L McIntyre; its audit specifically labels Original Source as modified Seti-UI MIT. Preserve both exact notices and modification/source records; do not flatten the aggregate's other accepted notices into either.

Custom _nf is a filename convention, not exclusive original authorship. Import chain mixes custom icons, retains older disappeared Seti forms as custom, drops duplicates/colored variants, chooses Seti Windows/Puppet and retains both C/C++ and folder alternatives. windows.svg still has i_custom_windows primary name; custom/seti aliases do not alter origin.

icons.tsv selects outlines and aliases; FontForge uniformly fits bounds53,0,947,900, centers, width1000, em1024, adds space, emits OTF then shifts generated i_seti mappings+0x100. Inkscape simplification precedes generation and substitutes only if output size is below80%; even dry mode invokes Inkscape and writes temp.svg. Workflow pins no dependency versions, compares regeneration with prior timestamp, conditionally regenerates/current-timestamps and commits. None executed.

unknowns.finding: Current Ruby bytes exactly equal the replacement in commit88eae283; its author describes converting an unnamed free pixel image to outlines. Source image URL/bytes, creator and applicable notice/terms are not identified in the bounded evidence. Free is not a rights grant, and _nf does not prove original artwork.
unknowns.nextAction: Before reuse publication, obtain the identified input image and exact source notice/authorization, or commission an independently created Ruby-role replacement with recorded origin and mapping/visual acceptance; root/user decides, no replacement authorized here.

releaseObligations.requirement: Preserve Firebase monochrome modification and recorded brand-usage conflict; preserve Bazel skeleton-to-filled-outline reconstruction attribution including Ezekiel Warren's idea and referenced upstream logo page. Source declarations do not settle trademark/brand usage; obtain an authorized publication decision or independent same-role replacement without dropping aliases/features.

Retain full Jesse Weed MIT and Ryan L McIntyre MIT texts with all previously accepted mixed-component notices and evidenced modifications. Do not substitute the application's adjacent OFL alone or relabel the whole Nerd aggregate MIT. Inspect shipped artifacts and accessible notices before publication.

Resolve SN-U1; keep unidentified historical attribution limits explicit. Hand-drawn Chuck claim is source-characterized by its commit and matching current bytes, not blanket authorship authentication of all custom glyphs.

executionDebt.requirement: Under later explicit authorization, reproduce the Original component with recorded FontForge/Inkscape/tool versions and controlled timestamps; compare glyph outlines, codepoints, aliases and metrics with pinned original-source.otf. Current generator3.4.0 versus component metadata3.3.0 prevents claiming its exact build was established.
executionDebt.assertionStatus: Reproducible-build obligation, not a product test pass.

executionDebt.requirement: Verify final aggregate and packaged renderer preserve all191 role mappings/21 aliases, including Windows and Seti/custom overlaps, C/C++, folders, old CSS versus new CSS; test native rendering, sizing/clipping and fallback. An exact Bicep raw-byte join does not substitute for this.
executionDebt.assertionStatus: Proposed acceptance assertions only; no new or original assertion body was executed or claimed inspected here.

executionDebt.requirement: Inspect distributable/application notice payloads and ensure source notices, modifications and accepted other components survive bundling; no package build or installation ran.

retained.sourceTestAllocation: unchanged; reuse frozen reports and root accepted font evidence
retained.features: All original glyph roles/languages/screenshots/journeys, platform/SSH/folder/mixed-version contracts retained; no feature or asset removed.
retained.phase: Actual Sol implementation remains gated on complete root source-audit acceptance.

declarations.message:
svgs: Add new css icon to custom set

We keep the Seti css logo, as the abstract hash tag is prone to 'misuse'
for other purposes and an update of the logo would break it. Anyhow CSS
shield is the current logo before the newly added one, and anyone who
used the Seti css logo (i.e. hash tag) would probably mean something
entirely different.

svgs: css: Simplify to path

[why]
Fontforge's cvs import sometimes struggles (hard) on transforms.

[how]
Apply the transform before saving. It's not that we want to edit it
anyhow, so no reason to keep that abstraction.

Also remove some meta-information.
feat(svgs): add css_new icon

Add Vitruvian Man icon

Fixes: #1001

Add chuck icon

Hand drawn in Inkscape.

Fixes: #1489

Update Ruby icon

[why]
Improve legibility by having gaps between the gemstone surfaces.

[how]
There is no official monochrome icon. Found one free pixel one and
converted that to outline.

Update Firebase icon from original icon

[why]
Improve legibility. The full icon is in fact a multicolor icon and the
design depends on being rendered in multiple different colors. That is
impossible for fonts. So we should probably use their flat (mono-color)
icon instead, which hints the different 'flaps' through gaps instead of
colors.

[note]
Both icons (the old and the new) contradict rules given by Firebase to
use the logo. But that can not be helped in a icon font, as we just have
one color of undetermined hue.

Update Bazel icon from original icon

[why]
The Bazel icon might look nicer with gaps between the surfaces of the
cubes.
That is halfway in-line with the design idea of their logo.

See PR #1610 and link
https://blog.bazel.build/2017/07/05/new-logo-and-homepage.html

[how]
Based on the idea from Ezekiel Warren the Bazel icon gets gaps between
the surfaces of the cubes.
For this we use the skeleton svg icon of the Bazel website and construct
from scratch a new outline to represent the cube surfaces. The original
svg used lines with a width to create the image, which is not compatible
to fonts.

[why]
We need the glyphnames to be unique, or some glyphs will not be
accessible later (in the cheat sheet, css, glyphnames).

[note]
Also already remove one non-effective duplicate that is first an alias
and later a real glyph in i_seti.sh
Update documentation
Actually use new Seti
Actually use new Seti

Clean up icon doubles

Some icons are now existing twice.

* Their crystal icon looks wrong (rotationwise), compare with https://github.com/crystal-lang/crystal
* Their C logo misses the standard's hex shape
* Their C++ logo misses the standard's hex shape
* Their Elixir icons has a dent in the reflextion?
* Their Elm icon is colored
* Their Git Folder is not a folder
* Their Kotlin icon is colored
* Their Puppet icon is more correct
* Their Pursescript icon is identical
* Their Windows icon is more modern

That means:

* Do not include their crystal, elixir, elm, kotlin, purescript
* Do not include our puppet, windows
* Keeping both c, c++, git-folder

[note]
Keeping their old files around with changed suffix to find this commit
in the future on updates.

Reuse old icons that were labeled as 'seti' but have been vanished as

And remove 'red' versions of icons. We have a black and white font...
